research_question: What is the causal effect of [TREATMENT] on [OUTCOME] for [POPULATION] in a general causal analysis workflow?
background: This comprehensive workflow framing document provides a structured template for conducting causal inference analyses across various domains and research questions. It encompasses the full causal analysis pipeline from problem formulation through validation and interpretation. The template is designed to be adaptable to different study designs, data structures, and causal estimands while maintaining rigorous methodological standards. It supports both experimental and observational settings, with appropriate assumptions and validation criteria for each approach.

variables.name: treatment
variables.description: Primary treatment or exposure variable of interest (1 = treated, 0 = control)
variables.measurement: Defined based on study context (e.g., intervention assignment, exposure assessment)

variables.name: outcome
variables.description: Primary outcome variable to be measured post-treatment
variables.measurement: Standardized measurement appropriate to outcome type

variables.name: outcome_binary
variables.description: Binary version of outcome for alternative analyses

variables.name: age
variables.description: Age of study participant in years

variables.name: socioeconomic_status
variables.description: Socioeconomic status based on composite measure

variables.name: baseline_outcome
variables.description: Pre-treatment measurement of the outcome variable

variables.name: comorbidity_index
variables.description: Comorbidity or risk factor summary score

variables.name: time_period
variables.description: Time period of observation or enrollment

variables.name: random_assignment
variables.description: Random assignment to treatment eligibility (for instrumental variable analysis)

variables.name: cluster_id
variables.description: Cluster identifier for clustered or hierarchical data

variables.name: weight
variables.description: Sampling or analysis weight for complex survey designs

estimand.description: Average treatment effect across the entire target population
estimand.target_population: All eligible units in the study population with complete data
estimand.estimand_justification: ATE chosen for population-level policy relevance, with alternatives available for specific research questions

study_design.description: Adaptable design supporting randomized experiments, quasi-experiments, and observational studies
study_design.assignment_mechanism: Varies by design: random assignment, natural experiment, or self-selection
study_design.data_collection_method: Flexible: primary data collection, secondary data analysis, or administrative records
study_design.cluster_handling: Supported for hierarchical or clustered data structures
study_design.missing_data_strategy: Multiple imputation, inverse probability weighting, or complete case analysis

assumptions.name: Conditional Exchangeability
assumptions.description: Treatment assignment is independent of potential outcomes given observed covariates
assumptions.test_method: Balance tests after adjustment, negative control outcomes, sensitivity analysis
assumptions.rationale: Core assumption for causal identification in observational studies

assumptions.name: Positivity
assumptions.description: Every unit has non-zero probability of receiving each treatment level given covariates
assumptions.test_method: Propensity score distribution analysis, overlap plots, minimum effective sample size
assumptions.rationale: Ensures comparable groups for causal estimation

assumptions.name: Consistency
assumptions.description: Potential outcome under observed treatment equals observed outcome
assumptions.test_method: Sensitivity analysis to treatment definitions, version analysis
assumptions.rationale: Links potential outcomes to observed data

assumptions.name: No Interference
assumptions.description: One unit's treatment does not affect another unit's outcome
assumptions.rationale: Ensures stable unit treatment value assumption (SUTVA)
assumptions.violations: Spillover effects, network effects, general equilibrium

assumptions.name: Correct Model Specification
assumptions.description: Statistical models correctly specify relationships between variables
assumptions.test_method: Residual analysis, goodness-of-fit tests, cross-validation, specification tests

assumptions.name: Independent Sampling
assumptions.description: Units are sampled independently from the target population
assumptions.alternatives: Cluster-robust standard errors, mixed effects models

assumptions.name: Instrument Exclusion
assumptions.description: Instrument affects outcome only through treatment

assumptions.name: Parallel Trends
assumptions.description: Treatment and control groups would have followed parallel trends without treatment

validation_criteria.name: Covariate Balance
validation_criteria.description: Covariates should be balanced across treatment groups after adjustment
validation_criteria.test: Love plots, balance tables, statistical tests

validation_criteria.name: Positivity Assessment
validation_criteria.description: Sufficient overlap in propensity scores across treatment groups

validation_criteria.name: Instrument Strength
validation_criteria.description: First-stage relationship between instrument and treatment

validation_criteria.name: Randomization Balance
validation_criteria.description: Baseline covariates balanced across randomized groups

validation_criteria.name: Parallel Trends Test
validation_criteria.description: Pre-treatment trends should be parallel between groups

validation_criteria.name: Model Diagnostics
validation_criteria.description: Statistical models should pass diagnostic checks
validation_criteria.threshold: No severe multicollinearity (VIF < 10), homoscedasticity, normality of residuals
validation_criteria.test: VIF analysis, residual plots, specification tests

validation_criteria.name: Sensitivity Analysis
validation_criteria.description: Estimates should be robust to reasonable unmeasured confounding
validation_criteria.test: E-value calculation, Rosenbaum bounds, bias analysis

validation_criteria.name: Placebo Tests
validation_criteria.description: No effect should be found for impossible outcomes or time periods
validation_criteria.test: Analysis with placebo outcomes or pre-treatment periods

validation_criteria.name: Falsification Tests
validation_criteria.description: Tests using known null effects should not reject null
validation_criteria.test: Analysis with outcomes known to be unaffected

sample_size.justification: Minimum for basic analysis, recommended for stable estimates, large-scale for subgroup analyses

time_periods.description: Number of observation periods required by design

data_requirements.data_structure: Individual-level dataset with one row per observation unit per time period
data_requirements.missing_data_policy: Systematic missing data assessment and appropriate handling

analysis_methods.name: Randomized Experiment Analysis
analysis_methods.description: Intention-to-treat and per-protocol analysis of randomized data
analysis_methods.limitations: May not be feasible or ethical for all questions

analysis_methods.name: Propensity Score Matching
analysis_methods.description: Match treated and control units on propensity scores
analysis_methods.advantages: Intuitive, creates comparable groups, reduces dimensionality
analysis_methods.limitations: Discards data, sensitive to model specification, requires overlap

analysis_methods.name: Inverse Probability Weighting
analysis_methods.description: Weight observations by inverse probability of treatment received
analysis_methods.advantages: Uses full sample, estimates population ATE, handles continuous treatments
analysis_methods.limitations: Sensitive to extreme weights, requires positivity

analysis_methods.name: Doubly Robust Methods
analysis_methods.description: Combine outcome regression with propensity scores
analysis_methods.advantages: Consistent if either model correct, flexible, efficient
analysis_methods.limitations: More complex, requires both models to be reasonable
assumptions: At least one of outcome or treatment model correct

analysis_methods.name: Instrumental Variables
analysis_methods.description: Use instruments to address unmeasured confounding
analysis_methods.advantages: Addresses unmeasured confounding, local causal identification
analysis_methods.limitations: LATE interpretation, requires valid instrument, weak instrument problems

analysis_methods.name: Regression Discontinuity
analysis_methods.limitations: Local effects only, requires sufficient data at cutoff

analysis_methods.name: Difference-in-Differences
analysis_methods.description: Compare changes over time between treatment and control groups
analysis_methods.advantages: Controls for time-invariant unobserved confounding, intuitive
analysis_methods.limitations: Requires parallel trends, sensitive to composition changes

analysis_methods.name: Synthetic Control
analysis_methods.description: Construct weighted combination of control units
analysis_methods.advantages: Data-driven control group, transparent weights, good for case studies
analysis_methods.limitations: Single treated unit, pre-treatment fit requirements

analysis_methods.name: Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation
analysis_methods.description: Semiparametric efficient estimation with machine learning
analysis_methods.advantages: Double robust, flexible, optimal bias-variance tradeoff

analysis_methods.name: Causal Forest Methods
analysis_methods.description: Machine learning for heterogeneous treatment effects
analysis_methods.advantages: Captures effect heterogeneity, nonparametric, honest estimation

limitations: Unmeasured confounding may bias observational estimates
Limited generalizability beyond study population and context
Measurement error in variables can bias estimates
Sample size constraints may limit power for subgroup analyses
Temporal ordering assumptions may be violated in cross-sectional data
Spillover effects and interference may violate SUTVA
Missing data mechanisms may introduce bias if not properly handled
Multiple testing and false discovery concerns in exploratory analyses
Computational complexity for advanced methods may limit practical application
ethical_considerations: Informed consent and privacy protection for human subjects
Fair and equitable treatment of all study participants
Transparent reporting of methods and limitations
Consideration of potential harms from research findings
Appropriate handling of sensitive demographic information
Consideration of algorithmic fairness in automated analyses
Responsible communication of uncertainty and limitations
Avoidance of stigmatization in reporting group differences
Consideration of policy implications and unintended consequences
quality_assurance: Pre-registration of analysis plans when possible
Documentation of all data processing decisions
Version control for analysis code and data
Peer review of methods and results
Validation of findings with external data when available
Regular quality checks for data integrity
author: Causal Analysis Workflow Template
